findings.summary: The bounding-surface colour is now a hardcoded hex literal '#6a4c93' in both the draw call (line 224) and the legend handle (line 281), replacing the named ink role DEFAULT_INK.separatrix_color. The rendered per-trip sheets are correct and the violet separates cleanly from the red axis, which is the defect the commit set out to fix; but nova's plotting rules require a figure colour to be a named role in the style module so the same component reads the same way across figures, and a literal in a prototype script silently diverges from that owner. This is the same finding the previous figure review recorded at this line and it is still open. The repair belongs in nova/media/ink.py (a named role, e.g. bounding-surface violet), outside this node's fence.

The commit states 'the legend no longer carries two red entries', and the per-trip sheets carry that; the two summary sheets (frame-137-flux-contours.png and frame-146-flux-contours.png) still do not. Their legends carry 'bounding surface (limited)' / 'no bounding surface (read refused)' as a red line beside the red 'solved axis' triangle and the red 'limiter contact' dot, so a reader of the summary sheet still has to hold the legend open to tell which red mark is which. The two sheets also still run their residual x-axis to trip 15 while the series stops at trip 4, so the 'residual axis sized to the trips run' half of the commit does not reach them either. Either the summary sheets are drawn by a path that does not apply the same colour and axis changes a reader sees on the per-trip sheets, or they were not re-rendered with this change.

The lower pane's y-axis carries only the tick values 0.00 and 0.25 and no axis label, so the figure does not name what the trace measures or in what unit. The x-axis is labelled 'active-set trip' and the poloidal panel is fully explained by its legend, so the lower pane is the one element a reader must guess at; the same is true of frame-146-trip-2 and frame-137-trip-2. An axis label naming the quantity beside its unit, as the library's own 'relative residual' label does on the summary sheets, would close it. Non-blocking because every per-trip sheet carries the same missing label rather than one sheet clipping it.

The lower pane marks the trip a sheet is about with a red dot, and immediately above that dot a small triangular glyph is drawn so close to the pane's top edge that it reads as a clipped marker rather than as a label. On frame-146-trip-1 and frame-146-trip-2 the same mark sits partly outside the plotting area. The mark carries no text, so a reader cannot tell whether it is an annotation of the highlighted trip or a stray artist; either place it inside the pane with clear space, or label it. Non-blocking because the highlighted trip is also the red dot and its identity is not lost.

The text 'mask difference above each point' floats in the upper right of the residual pane, far from the curve in the upper left, and the bare numerals printed above the curve (27, 40, 1, 0, 0 here; 24, 20, 9, 9, 0 on the frame-137 summary) are given no key inside the figure. Nothing ties the phrase to the numerals but their position, so a reader meets a title for data that is not in that corner and cannot confirm the numerals are mask entries changed. The commit states 'each caption now states the mask entries changed on its trip', which fixes this for the per-trip sheets; the summary sheets still carry the unkeyed form.

The poloidal panel occupies roughly a third of the canvas width and is centred, so the sheet spends most of its ink on white margin at the left and right while the flux field the page exists to show is drawn small. The contours near the top of the panel are cut off where the grid domain bound ends, which is faithful to the data, but at this panel size the cut reads as a cropping of the figure rather than as the domain edge. A larger poloidal panel on a narrower canvas would let a reader see the escape and the closed-cell count the caption claims. Non-blocking: the caption states the count and the axis position, so the information is not lost, only harder to see.
